citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team (2025). ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952.
creator: Chenchen Zhang, Yuhang Li, Can Xu, Jiaheng Liu, Ao Liu, Changzhi Zhou, Ken Deng, Dengpeng Wu, Guanhua Huang, Kejiao Li, Qi Yi, Ruibin Xiong, Shihui Hu, Yue Zhang, Yuhao Jiang, Zenan Xu, Yuanxing Zhang, Wiggin Zhou, Chayse Zhou, Fengzong Lian (Tencent Hunyuan Team)
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark of 1,825 diverse tasks for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation. It covers nine domains (Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others), stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers. The benchmark is paired with an automated, multimodal evaluation pipeline that renders artifacts, captures three-step temporal screenshots, and uses a checklist-guided MLLM-as-Judge to assess visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality.
name: ArtifactsBench
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each query is paired with one 10-dimension checklist. For human validation, multiple front-end engineers independently scored each of the 280 sampled queries; the final human ground-truth score is the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human validators for the 280-instance expert study were described as engineers with extensive front-end development experience. No further demographic details (nationality, age, gender) are provided.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 was achieved among annotators on the 10% manually curated seed set used for checklist calibration. A 280-instance double-blind human expert study (6 models, multiple front-end engineers) measured pairwise agreement (Pair ACC) between the automated MLLM referee and human judges, achieving up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with Gemini-2.5-Pro as referee.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom in-house pipeline; no third-party annotation platform (e.g., Mechanical Turk) is mentioned. Execution uses headless Chromium via Playwright at 1024×768 resolution for artifact rendering and screenshot capture.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted (by Hunyuan-Turbos) and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. The 10 items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions. Solvability validation collected candidate solutions from multiple model families; tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed.
rai:dataBiases: License-violating items were explicitly filtered out during sourcing. De-duplication (MinHash + semantic similarity + perceptual hashing) was applied to avoid near-duplicate tasks. Difficulty was calibrated post hoc using aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs rather than a priori assignment, to preserve discriminative power and avoid difficulty bias. Tasks solvable only by brittle hacks (e.g., hard-coded coordinates) were revised or removed to avoid rewarding non-generalizable solutions.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). The curated pool was then seeded for further expansion via a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw sources include expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and screenshots used for LLM visual-to-query generation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: 1) The three-step screenshot approach may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (e.g., multi-step user workflows, nuanced physics in games). 2) The benchmark evaluates only single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic, iterative, or multi-turn development capabilities. 3) Discrete screenshot sampling may miss subtle dynamic behaviors between captured frames.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs to enforce a 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split (realized as 559/611/655), stable under leave-family-out resampling. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Two-stage de-duplication: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. A lightweight classifier with human spot-checks assigned sub-category tags.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains (stated in Appendix A.4).
rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench provides a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models. By enabling automated, holistic evaluation of interactive visual artifacts, it aims to bridge the gap between static code correctness benchmarks and real-world user experience quality, supporting progress in LLM-driven web and application development.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLMs on their ability to generate high-quality, executable interactive visual artifacts (web widgets, data visualizations, mini-games, simulations, SVG graphics, management systems, multimedia editors). Benchmarking and ranking LLMs for visual code generation. Providing fine-grained diagnostic insights into model strengths and failure modes across interactivity levels and task categories.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos was used to LLM-draft checklists. Gemini-2.5-Pro was used to classify queries into categories (Appendix A.7). A lightweight classifier was used for sub-category tagging with human spot-checks. During evaluation, Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B serve as dual MLLM-as-Judge referees. MinHash was used for semantic de-duplication; perceptual hashing was used for visual de-duplication.
